name: Pradhan Mantri Kaushal Vikas Yojana - Recognition Of Prior Learning
nodalDept: Ministry Of Skill Development And Entrepreneurship
briefDescription: PMKVY Recognition of Prior Learning (RPL) lets working Indians aged 18–45 get an official government-backed skill certificate for knowledge they already have, without classroom training — by passing a direct assessment.
descriptionMd:
Recognition of Prior Learning (RPL) is a certification component under Pradhan Mantri Kaushal Vikas Yojana (PMKVY), run by the Ministry of Skill Development & Entrepreneurship. It acknowledges the informal skills that millions of Indians have built up through years of on-the-job experience — and converts that experience into a formal, recognised qualification.

RPL is particularly aimed at workers in **unregulated, informal sectors** — construction, agriculture, domestic help, small trades — who have never had the opportunity to obtain a formal certificate but are already skilled practitioners. The assessment is conducted by Sector Skill Councils (SSCs), and candidates who pass receive a PMKVY certificate that improves their employability and opens doors to formal employment.
benefitsMd:
- A **nationally recognised skill certificate** under the PMKVY framework, issued after a competency-based assessment by the relevant Sector Skill Council.
- **Bridge training** (short orientation, 12–80 hours) provided where needed to fill small knowledge gaps before the final assessment — at no cost to the candidate.
- **Direct benefit transfer** of the stipend/incentive amount to the candidate's Aadhaar-linked bank account.
- Improved access to **formal employment, higher wages and career progression** backed by a recognised credential.
eligibilityMd:
- Indian citizen aged **18 to 45 years**.
- Has **prior work experience** in the job role for which RPL certification is sought — the minimum experience requirement is set by each Sector Skill Council (SSC) for that specific role.
- Possesses an **Aadhaar card** and an **Aadhaar-linked bank account**.
- Any additional criteria (such as the number of years of experience) are defined by the SSC for the relevant trade.
applicationMd:
RPL candidates are enrolled through **Sector Skill Councils (SSCs)** or their authorised Project Implementing Agencies (PIAs). The process:

**Step 1:** Find the SSC responsible for your trade (e.g., Construction Skill Council for mason/carpenter, Domestic Workers Sector Skill Council for household workers).
**Step 2:** Register on the **Skill India Digital Hub** ([skillindiadigital.gov.in](https://www.skillindiadigital.gov.in/)) and search for RPL opportunities in your trade.
**Step 3:** Attend the **Pre-Screening or Bridge Training** (if required by the SSC for your job role).
**Step 4:** Appear for the **competency-based assessment** conducted by the SSC or a third-party Assessment Body.
**Step 5:** On passing, your certificate is issued digitally and the stipend/incentive is transferred to your bank account.
